The best 3-qubit chain on garnet right now is QB7-QB12-QB11. QB12 is the middle qubit.

How I found it: I read garnet's current default calibration set (f81c45da-6e73-4b5d-a0fe-72c75635fade). It has an interleaved randomized benchmarking (IRB) fidelity for all 28 CZ pairs, using the default CZ implementation (slepian_crf). I checked every chain where qubit b is paired with both a and c, and I multiplied the two fidelities for each chain.
- The CZ fidelity of QB7-QB12 is 0.99802.
- The CZ fidelity of QB12-QB11 is 0.99869.
- Their product is 0.99671.
- The next best chain is QB12-QB11-QB16, with a product of 0.99469.

What I ran: I ran a 3-qubit GHZ circuit on garnet:mock with 200 shots. Job ID: 01a160a5-498b-74d6-ab4f-91b0c124db2d. The circuit puts all three qubits into an equal mix of 0 and 1. It then applies one CZ on QB12-QB7 and one CZ on QB12-QB11. It then rotates QB7 and QB11 back and measures all three qubits. I read the circuit back from the server. It had exactly 2 CZ gates, and it measured QB7, QB12 and QB11. A noise-free simulation of this exact circuit gives 50% 000 and 50% 111.

What the numbers show: the mock returned 000: 57, 001: 58, 110: 48 and 111: 37. These counts do not look like a GHZ state. That is expected. The mock checks that the circuit is valid for garnet, but its counts are random and do not depend on the circuit. The mock also used its own calibration set (f04fe114-002f-46bd-8fa4-2a577ff56501), not the real garnet one. On the real garnet QPU you would expect mostly 000 and 111.

The principle: a GHZ state links three qubits so that measuring them gives all zeros or all ones, and never a mix. Each CZ gate adds some error, so choosing the pairs with the best CZ fidelity gives the cleanest GHZ result on real hardware. This mock run cost 0 credits.
